title: New York in the 1970s

description.main: Black-and-white photographs of Manhattan architecture by Philip Trager, made in the 1970s and printed from rediscovered negatives. Steidl, text by Stephen C. Pinson.
description.extended:
Philip Trager's architectural photographs of Manhattan from the 1970s, printed from negatives that had gone unprinted for decades.

The book, with text by Stephen C. Pinson, shows buildings in sharp detail as what the publisher calls "place portraiture". Trager chose his subjects for visual reasons rather than documentary ones, though the pictures now also serve as a record of the city. He made them at the same time as the work in Philip Trager: New York (Wesleyan University Press, 1980), but this selection turns more to how the architecture meets the street. The negatives were only recently rediscovered, and no prints had been made from them at the time.

Trager (b. 1935) is known for photographs of architecture and of dancers in outdoor settings, and lives in Connecticut.

notes: Year 2015 per Getty MARC 260; D.A.P. pub date 10/25/2016. Pages Getty 111, D.A.P. 112.
